checkpoints.description: [1/5] Widen SECRET_PATTERNS with prefixed high-confidence credential shapes and extend the private-key block to ENCRYPTED and SSH2 headers. [2/5] Add scrub_text(text) -> (scrubbed, detectors) using pattern detection only, never the entropy fallback, so prose keeps its hashes and digests. [3/5] disruption_recovery --checkpoint refuses credential-shaped free text and names --redact as the fix; --redact scrubs and writes. [4/5] subagent_delegate always scrubs the sub-agent's returned text and its JSON output. [5/5] README, data_models, ADR, map and sync refresh, then every Phase 4 gate.

impact_assessment.why: PRINCIPLE-019 R5 makes a leaked credential unrecoverable: it must be rotated, never reverted. The scanner already catches 15 shapes and already reads both ledgers and the dogfood log, but it only reports after the text is on disk, and the ledger's --why/--benefits/--risks/--mitigation fields are written straight into a git-tracked file. Blocking the write is worth more than reporting it afterwards, and the pattern table misses common prefixed formats (GitLab, npm, PyPI, SendGrid, HuggingFace, Telegram, Notion, Azure AccountKey and others).
impact_assessment.benefits: A credential quoted in an impact note is refused before it reaches a tracked file rather than found after; sub-agent output cannot carry a key into the lead agent's context or any downstream log; the pattern table roughly doubles while keeping the near-zero false-positive property the file's own design depends on.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --checkpoint gains a refusal path and a --redact flag, so a script writing credential-shaped free text now exits non-zero; existing checkpoint text is unaffected. dependency: none, re and the scanner are already imported where needed. concurrency: the refusal happens before the file lock is taken, so no partial write is possible. state: no schema change; scrubbing alters only the free-text field values that --redact is explicitly asked to rewrite.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add only prefixed shapes with literal anchors, never bare-length or PII patterns, and never apply the entropy fallback to prose, so legitimate commit hashes and digests in a risk note still pass; add a failing-first test per new pattern and per wiring point; make the refusal name --redact in its Fix line; scrub with a placeholder the STRONG_ALLOWLIST already recognizes so a scrubbed ledger stays clean on rescan.

[1/5] parse_handoff(text): pure parser and validator for 'state: ...; next: ...; failed: ...; open: ...; evidence: ...', mirroring the RISK_DIMENSIONS convention; next is required, an unknown key exits 2, total bounded to 2000 chars. [2/5] Store it as an optional handoff object on the checkpoint through record_checkpoint, with no schema version bump, and route its text through the ADR-173 credential gate. [3/5] --handoff on both CLI surfaces through the one checkpoint_command path. [4/5] format_resume_report prints the active task's latest handoff and uses its next value in place of the hardcoded Next Action line, inside PRINCIPLE-004 R5's 100-line budget. [5/5] README, data_models, ADR-174, map and sync refresh, then every Phase 4 gate.

impact_assessment.why: Resuming this session's own interrupted task required reading a git diff to learn which of six milestones were done, because the ledger records the plan but nothing about progress against it, nothing tried and abandoned, and nothing awaiting the user. format_resume_report's Next Action line is a hardcoded generic string, so the cold-start report tells every task the same thing. A question put to the user this session would have been lost to compaction with nowhere to record it.
impact_assessment.benefits: A resumed agent reads what was done, what failed, what is still open and what to do next instead of re-deriving it from a diff; the cold-start Next Action becomes task-specific; an unanswered user question survives compaction. One flag, one parser, consistent with the --risks format the kit already validates.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: --checkpoint and aikit checkpoint gain an optional --handoff flag and checkpoints gain an optional handoff key; no existing field changes and no reader is required to understand it. dependency: none. concurrency: none, the write stays inside the existing lock. state: deliberately NO ledger schema version bump; validate_ledger_version refuses any version that is not exactly LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION, including older ones, so bumping to 2 would make AIKit's own ledger and all 20 projects' ledgers unreadable. The change is purely additive, so an older build ignores the new key harmlessly.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the field optional and absent-by-default so every existing ledger stays valid and every reader uses .get(); bound the parsed text and refuse unknown keys so the packet cannot grow into a second description field; scrub it with the ADR-173 gate so it cannot become a new credential surface; add failing-first tests for the parser, the round-trip through a v1 ledger, and the resume rendering; report the validate_ledger_version asymmetry to the user rather than fixing it inside this task (PRINCIPLE-007 R4).

The purpose is to afford the runbook pointer: the operational runbook in .agents/skills/aikit/SKILL.md is auto-discovered by only 2 of the 8 supported hosts and no Tier 1 file references it, so every rule placed there is invisible to the other 6, and ADR-175 measured that the pointer did not fit in the 3 characters the old budget left.

impact_assessment.risks: contract: the numeric limit in PRINCIPLE-001 R6 changes, which TestRuleNumberParity pins against the code constant, and all 8 generated host surfaces grow by one line and about 150 tokens of allowance. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: no schema or persisted data changes; the Tier 1B 1,200-character adopter allowance is untouched, so no adopter loses room.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Update the code constant and every document that states the number in the same commit so the parity test stays green; recompute and state the 90% advisory warning rather than leaving a stale 1,440; add a test asserting every Tier 1 target names the skill path so the pointer cannot silently vanish; name PRINCIPLE-001's full citing set in ADR-176; verify the measured margin after the change rather than asserting it.

checkpoints.description: Task 'review-findings-remediation-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] ui finish: when review is the only blocker, say so and drop the revert/allow/abort advice; exit code and the ui.review-missing JSON code unchanged. [2/3] check_reachability: delete the dead all_literals fallback, correct its comment to the strict behaviour, and pin with a regression test that a producer hidden in a comprehension is flagged. [3/3] Ledger version: accept 1 <= version <= current on both read and write, still refusing < 1, newer and non-int; align data_models.md; ADR-178 recording the 27-ledger correction to ADR-174.

impact_assessment.why: Three findings reproduced end to end. ui finish tells a user whose change verify just passed that it is outside its contract and leads with abort, which reverts the work. The reachability fallback is dead because a set cannot count above 1, and its comment describes a weaker behaviour that would have passed a hidden producer this session. validate_ledger_version and save_ledger refuse every version but the current one, so the first schema bump makes all 27 v1 ledgers unreadable and migrate_ledger_schema can never run.
impact_assessment.benefits: A user blocked only on review is told exactly that and keeps their work; the safety gate keeps its strict behaviour without a comment inviting someone to weaken it; a future schema bump can migrate existing ledgers instead of stopping every ledger command across 27 ledgers.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: finish's human stderr text changes in the review-only case, exit code 1 and JSON codes unchanged; the ledger accepts older valid versions, but with LEDGER_SCHEMA_VERSION 1 that is identical to today. dependency: none. concurrency: none. state: no ledger is rewritten; acceptance widens only below the current version and all existing refusals (True, '2', 2.0, 0, -1, newer) stay.
impact_assessment.mitigation: A failing-first test per milestone; reproduce the finish message against a real sandbox project; keep test_invalid_ledger_versions_are_refused unchanged and green; change both version checks through one shared predicate so they cannot drift; commit each milestone separately after its Phase 4 passes, per PRINCIPLE-006 R1.
